a-march.name: A-march
a-march.short: A slow marching drill that teaches the sprinting leg action one step at a time.
how: Stand tall, up on the balls of the feet.
Drive one knee up to hip height, toe pulled up toward the shin.
Put the foot straight back down under the hip, not out in front.
Walk forward doing this, alternating legs.
a-march.watch: Leaning back, or the foot reaching out in front of the body on the way down.
a-march.cue: Knee up, foot down under you, stay tall.

animal-walk-medley.name: Animal walk medley
animal-walk-medley.short: A string of animal crawls back to back, the standing warm-up of this program.
how: Pick five animals: bear, crab, monkey, flamingo, giraffe.
Do about 10m of each with no rest between.
Change the order day to day so it stays a game.
animal-walk-medley.watch: Rushing. Slow and strong beats fast and floppy every time.
animal-walk-medley.cue: Be the animal, not a kid in a hurry.

arm-circles.name: Arm circles
arm-circles.short: Shoulder warm-up, small circles growing into big ones, both directions.
how: Arms straight out to the sides.
Ten small circles forward, then ten big ones.
Repeat both sizes backward.
arm-circles.watch: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
arm-circles.cue: Draw circles on the wall behind you.

athletic-stance.name: Athletic stance
athletic-stance.short: The ready shape every sport starts from: feet wide, knees soft, weight forward.
how: Feet a bit wider than the shoulders.
Bend the knees and push the hips back slightly.
Chest up, hands out in front, weight on the balls of the feet.
athletic-stance.watch: Straight legs, or weight sitting back on the heels.

bear-walk.name: Bear walk
bear-walk.short: Crawling on hands and feet with the hips high and the knees off the ground.
how: Hands under the shoulders, feet under the hips, knees hovering just off the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot together.
Keep the hips level and travel forward.
bear-walk.watch: Knees dropping to the floor, or the hips rocking side to side.
bear-walk.cue: Flat back, like a table you could put a drink on.

between-point-reset.name: Between-point reset
between-point-reset.short: A three-part routine after every point that clears the last one and starts the next.
how: Breathe out once, slowly.
Bounce the ball a set number of times, the same number every time.
Look at the strings, then look up and play.
Same routine after a winner and after a double fault.
between-point-reset.watch: Skipping it when he is annoyed. That is the exact moment it is worth the most.

bounce-pass.name: Bounce pass
bounce-pass.short: The same push as a chest pass, aimed at the floor about two thirds of the way to the target.
how: Same grip and step as the chest pass.
Aim the bounce about two thirds of the distance to the receiver.
The ball should arrive at their waist, not their ankles.
bounce-pass.watch: Bouncing it too close to himself, which makes the ball arrive too high and slow.
bounce-pass.cue: Bounce it two thirds of the way.

broad-jump.name: Broad jump
broad-jump.short: A two-footed jump for distance from a standing start.
how: Toes behind the line, feet about hip width.
Swing both arms back and bend the knees.
Throw the arms forward and jump out as far as possible.
It only counts if the landing is stuck.
broad-jump.watch: Falling forward or stepping after landing. Measure to the back heel.
broad-jump.cue: Arms back, then throw them at the horizon.

build-up-runs.name: Build-up runs
build-up-runs.short: Gradual runs that ramp from easy to nearly fast, used to warm up before anything quick.
how: Over 20m, start easy and get smoothly faster.
First run about 60 percent, second 70, third 80.
Walk back between each one.
build-up-runs.watch: Starting at full speed. These are the ramp, not the race.
build-up-runs.cue: Roll into it like a plane taking off.

bunny-hops.name: Bunny hops
bunny-hops.short: Hands on a line, both feet kicked over to the other side and landed together. Cartwheel step 1.
how: Chalk a line on the ground.
Put both hands flat on the line, arms straight.
Kick both feet up and over to the other side of the line.
Land with the feet together. Ten each direction.
bunny-hops.watch: Bent arms, or looking at his feet instead of his hands.
bunny-hops.cue: Arms straight, look at your hands.

cartwheel-step-1.name: Cartwheel step 1
cartwheel-step-1.short: The first rung of the cartwheel ladder: bunny hops over a line, getting used to weight on the hands.
how: Hands on a chalk line, arms locked straight.
Kick both feet over the line together and land on the other side.
Build up to hips rising above the shoulders.
cartwheel-step-1.watch: Arms folding. Weight on the hands is the skill being built.

cartwheel-step-2.name: Cartwheel step 2
cartwheel-step-2.short: Four beats along a line: hand, hand, foot, foot. The cartwheel rhythm without the height.
how: Stand at the end of a chalk line and lunge forward.
Reach one hand onto the line, then the other, both on the line.
Kick one foot over, then the other, landing back on the line.
Eight each side. Say the four beats out loud.
cartwheel-step-2.watch: Hands landing off the line, or both feet leaving at once. It is four separate beats.

cartwheel-step-3.name: Cartwheel step 3
cartwheel-step-3.short: Starting the cartwheel from a proper standing lunge instead of from a crouch.
how: Stand tall at the line, arms up by the ears.
Step into a long lunge with the front knee bent.
Reach down the line hand, hand, and kick through foot, foot.
Finish standing, facing back the way you came.
cartwheel-step-3.watch: Dropping the chest before the lunge, which turns it back into step 2.
cartwheel-step-3.cue: Arms by your ears, then reach down the line.

champions-log.name: Champion's Log
champions-log.short: Teddy's own notebook, one line a day, written by him.
how: At the end of a session, he writes one line.
Either the best thing today, or what he wants to do tomorrow.
It belongs to him. Dad reads it only when invited.
champions-log.watch: Turning it into homework. One line is the whole ask.

chest-pass.name: Chest pass
chest-pass.short: A two-handed pass pushed straight from the chest to a target.
how: Ball at the chest, elbows in, thumbs behind it.
Step toward the target and push both arms straight.
Finish with the thumbs turned down and the palms facing out.
chest-pass.watch: Winding up behind the head first, which is slow and easy to read.

collapse-dive.name: Collapse dive
collapse-dive.short: The first diving progression, folding sideways to the ground from low rather than leaping.
how: Start kneeling on a mat, ball placed an arm's length to the side.
Fold sideways and land on the side of the leg, then the hip, then the shoulder.
Both hands on the ball, top hand behind it.
Progress from kneeling to sitting to squatting before ever doing it standing.
collapse-dive.watch: Landing on the elbow or the point of the hip. It lands leg, hip, shoulder, in that order.

cone-gate.name: Cone gate
cone-gate.short: Two cones set a short distance apart making a little goal to pass or dribble through.
how: Set two cones about a metre apart.
Pass or dribble the ball cleanly through the middle.
Narrow the gate as it gets easy.
Scatter several gates around for a dribbling course.
cone-gate.watch: Aiming at a cone instead of at the space between them.
cone-gate.cue: Through the middle, not at the cones.

cone-weave.name: Cone weave
cone-weave.short: Dribbling in and out of a line of cones, tested for time.
how: Five cones, two metres apart.
Weave out using the right hand, weave back using the left.
Ball stays below the waist, eyes up.
Two trials, record the best.
cone-weave.watch: Swinging wide around the cones. Tight turns are the skill.
cone-weave.cue: Close to the cones, low and quick.

contact-in-front.name: Contact in front
contact-in-front.short: Meeting the ball out in front of the body rather than beside or behind it.
how: Set up so the ball arrives in front of the lead hip.
Arm extended comfortably, not jammed against the body.
If the ball gets behind him, the fix is usually footwork, not the swing.
contact-in-front.watch: Late contact beside the hip. That is the first sign the ball is too fast or the split step was missed.
contact-in-front.cue: Hit it where you can see it.

crab-walk.name: Crab walk
crab-walk.short: Belly up, hands and feet on the ground, hips lifted, walking in any direction.
how: Sit down, hands behind you with fingers pointing at your feet.
Push the hips up until the body is a flat bridge.
Walk forward, backward and sideways without letting the hips sag.
crab-walk.watch: The bottom dragging along the floor. That means the hips gave up.

crossover.name: Crossover
crossover.short: Bouncing the ball across the body from one hand to the other.
how: Stay low in athletic stance.
Push the ball across the body, bouncing it just in front of the feet.
Catch it with the other hand and immediately push it back.
Twenty five, eyes up.
crossover.watch: Standing up, or the bounce going too wide where a defender could take it.
crossover.cue: Low and quick, right in front of you.

dead-hang.name: Dead hang
dead-hang.short: Hanging from a bar with straight arms for as long as possible.
how: Grip the bar with the thumbs wrapped around it, not alongside the fingers.
Arms straight, shoulders active rather than fully slumped.
Hang until the grip gives out. Best of two, two minutes rest between.
dead-hang.watch: Thumbs not wrapped, or swinging to buy time.

defensive-slides.name: Defensive slides
defensive-slides.short: Shuffling sideways in a low defensive stance with the hands active.
how: Feet wide, knees bent, hands out at waist height.
Push off the back foot, step with the lead foot, stay low.
Never let the feet cross or click together.
defensive-slides.watch: Standing up between slides, or bouncing up and down.
defensive-slides.cue: Nose behind the ball, never stand up.

donkey-kicks.name: Donkey kicks
donkey-kicks.short: Hands on the floor near a wall, kicking the hips and feet up toward it. Handstand preparation.
how: Hands flat on the floor about a foot from the wall.
Push off one foot and kick both heels up toward the wall.
Let the feet come straight back down under control.
Ten reps, going a bit higher each time.
donkey-kicks.watch: Bent arms, or crashing the feet into the wall. Control on the way down matters more than height.
donkey-kicks.cue: Push the ground away and float the hips up.

dribble-tag.name: Dribble tag
dribble-tag.short: A tag game where everyone keeps dribbling, with Dad stationary this fall.
how: Teddy dribbles inside a marked square.
Dad stays in one spot and rolls a second ball to try to tag him.
If Teddy loses his dribble, that counts as tagged.
Shrink the square to make it harder.
dribble-tag.watch: Head dropping when it gets hard. That is the thing the game is teaching.
dribble-tag.cue: Eyes up even when you are being chased.

drop-feed.name: Drop feed
drop-feed.short: The simplest feed there is: he drops the ball himself and hits it after the bounce.
how: Stand side on, already turned.
Drop the ball out in front of the lead foot.
Let it bounce up and hit it at the top of the bounce.
Twenty forehands, twenty backhands.
drop-feed.watch: Dropping the ball too close to the body, which forces a cramped swing.
drop-feed.cue: Drop it where you want to hit it.

figure-8.name: Figure 8
figure-8.short: Weaving the ball in a figure of eight around and between both legs.
how: Feet wide, knees bent, back fairly flat.
Pass the ball from the right hand, through the legs, to the left hand behind.
Bring it around the outside of the left leg and back through.
Ten each direction, then reverse.
figure-8.watch: Looking down at the ball, which is the whole habit being trained out.
figure-8.cue: Eyes on my fingers, not the ball.

finish-over-the-shoulder.name: Finish over the shoulder
finish-over-the-shoulder.short: Ending the swing with the racket up over the opposite shoulder, which proves the low-to-high path.
how: Start the swing below the ball.
Brush up through it.
Let the racket carry all the way through and finish beside the opposite ear.
Hold the finish for a second before resetting.
finish-over-the-shoulder.watch: Stopping the racket at the ball. A short finish usually means he is steering it.
finish-over-the-shoulder.cue: Catch the racket by your ear.

first-touch.name: First touch
first-touch.short: The very first contact after receiving, used to kill the ball's speed and set up the next move.
how: Meet the ball with the inside of the foot, ankle locked.
Let the foot give a little as the ball arrives, like catching an egg.
Push the ball half a metre into space, not straight back at the feet.
first-touch.watch: A stiff foot that bounces the ball away, or a touch that leaves it stuck under his body.
first-touch.cue: Soft foot, look up after the touch.

flamingo-walk.name: Flamingo walk
flamingo-walk.short: Slow walking with a pause standing on one leg at every step.
how: Step forward and rise onto one leg, the other knee lifted to hip height.
Hold still for two seconds.
Step through to the other leg and hold again.
flamingo-walk.watch: Hopping through the hold. The balance moment is the whole exercise.
flamingo-walk.cue: Freeze like a statue on one leg.

form-shooting.name: Form shooting
form-shooting.short: Close-range shooting with one hand under the ball, built purely for shape.
how: Stand one metre from the basket.
Shooting hand under the ball, guide hand on the side and doing nothing.
Elbow under the ball, shoot up and let the wrist flop down.
Hold the finish until the ball lands.
form-shooting.watch: Guide hand pushing, or throwing from the chest because the basket is too high. Lower the hoop before lowering the standard.
form-shooting.cue: Reach into the cookie jar and hold it.

gallops.name: Gallops
gallops.short: Sideways or forward skipping where the same foot always leads, like a horse.
how: Pick a lead foot and step out with it.
Let the back foot chase up to it without passing it.
Go 15m, then switch the lead foot.
gallops.watch: The back foot crossing past the lead foot, which turns it into running.
gallops.cue: One foot is the boss, the other one chases.

giraffe-walk.name: Giraffe walk
giraffe-walk.short: Walking tall on the toes with the arms stretched straight overhead.
how: Reach both arms up as high as they go.
Rise onto the toes and walk with long slow steps.
Stay stretched the whole time.
giraffe-walk.watch: Heels dropping, or arms falling to shoulder height.

green-ball.name: Green ball
green-ball.short: The transition ball at 75 percent of normal pressure, the default rally ball this year.
how: Bounces lower and travels slower than a yellow ball.
At his height it lets him meet the ball between waist and shoulder, which is where good form is built.
Yellow stays gated on skill, not on age.
green-ball.watch: Nothing to watch here, this is a reference entry.

hanging-knee-tucks.name: Hanging knee tucks
hanging-knee-tucks.short: Hanging from a bar and pulling both knees up toward the chest.
how: Dead hang with straight arms.
Pull both knees up toward the chest without swinging.
Lower them slowly back down.
hanging-knee-tucks.watch: Kicking and swinging to get the knees up. Slow down instead.

high-knees.name: High knees
high-knees.short: The A-march done at a quick running tempo over a short distance.
how: Same shape as the A-march: tall posture, knees to hip height, foot down under the hip.
Now do it quickly, covering ground slowly.
Short bouts of 10 to 15m.
high-knees.watch: Bending at the waist, or feet slapping the ground.

hollow-hold.name: Hollow hold
hollow-hold.short: Lying on the back in a shallow banana shape with shoulders and legs off the floor.
how: Lie on the back, arms overhead, legs straight.
Press the lower back flat into the floor.
Lift the shoulders and the legs a few inches and hold.
Fifteen seconds, twice.
hollow-hold.watch: A gap under the lower back. If it lifts, bend the knees or lower the legs.
hollow-hold.cue: Squeeze everything, back glued to the floor.

horse.name: HORSE
horse.short: The shooting game: match the other player's made shot or take a letter.
how: Dad calls a shot and takes it from one fixed spot.
If he makes it, Teddy has to make the same shot or take a letter.
First to spell HORSE loses. Use a handicap so it stays close.
horse.watch: Nothing technical. This is a competing game, and losing well is part of the point.

inchworms.name: Inchworms
inchworms.short: Bending to the floor, walking the hands out to a plank, then walking the feet up to the hands.
how: From standing, bend and put both hands on the floor.
Walk the hands out until the body is a straight plank.
Leave the hands still and take small steps with the feet up to the hands.
Stand up and repeat.
inchworms.watch: Hips sagging in the plank position.
inchworms.cue: Long body in the middle, no banana back.

inside-foot-pass.name: Inside-foot pass
inside-foot-pass.short: The basic accurate pass, struck with the flat inside of the foot.
how: Plant the non-kicking foot beside the ball, pointing at the target.
Turn the kicking foot out and lock the ankle.
Strike through the middle of the ball with the flat inside of the foot.
Follow through at the target.
inside-foot-pass.watch: A floppy ankle, or the plant foot pointing somewhere other than the target.
inside-foot-pass.cue: Lock the ankle, point the plant foot where it's going.

inside-hook.name: Inside hook
inside-hook.short: A turn that hooks the ball back across the body with the inside of the foot.
how: Run at the ball as if continuing forward.
Reach the foot past the ball and hook it back with the inside.
Turn the body with it and accelerate away.
inside-hook.watch: Slowing down before the turn, which tells a defender exactly what is coming.
inside-hook.cue: Sell it, then hook it back.

jump-rope.name: Jump rope
jump-rope.short: Basic single-unders: one rope pass per jump, counting the streak.
how: Rope behind the heels, elbows in close to the ribs.
Turn the rope with the wrists, not the whole arm.
Tiny hops, barely off the floor, landing on the balls of the feet.
Count consecutive jumps until a miss.
jump-rope.watch: Big arm circles and big jumps, the two things that end a streak.

jump-stop.name: Jump stop
jump-stop.short: Stopping from a dribble by landing on both feet at exactly the same time.
how: Dribble at a jog.
Hop off one foot and land on both feet together, knees bent.
Land balanced and still. Because both feet landed together, either foot can now be the pivot.
jump-stop.watch: One foot landing first. Then only the other foot can pivot, and it is a travel if he picks the wrong one.
jump-stop.cue: Both feet, same moment, stick it.

keeper-ready-position.name: Keeper ready position
keeper-ready-position.short: The goalkeeper's set stance, taken just as the shooter strikes the ball.
how: Feet a little wider than the shoulders, weight on the balls of the feet.
Knees bent, hips slightly back, chest forward over the toes.
Hands up in front at chest height, palms facing the ball.
Be still at the moment of the strike, not moving.
keeper-ready-position.watch: Hands down by the hips, or being caught mid-step when the shot comes.
keeper-ready-position.cue: Hands up, still feet, be set when he hits it.

line-touch.name: Line-touch
line-touch.short: A shuttle test: sprint 5m, touch, sprint back, touch, sprint out again.
how: Put cones at 0 and 5m.
Sprint out, touch the line with a hand, sprint back, touch, sprint out through the far cone.
Two trials, full rest, record the best.
line-touch.watch: Rounding the turn instead of stopping and touching. The braking is the point.
line-touch.cue: Low on the turns, hand all the way down.

med-ball-chest-pass.name: Med ball chest pass
med-ball-chest-pass.short: Throwing a light medicine ball from the chest at a wall or to Dad.
how: Hold the ball at chest height, elbows in.
Step forward and push it out hard with both hands.
Finish with the arms straight and the palms turned out.
med-ball-chest-pass.watch: Using a ball that is too heavy, which turns a fast push into a slow heave.
med-ball-chest-pass.cue: Push it like you mean it.

monkey-walk.name: Monkey walk
monkey-walk.short: A wide squat waddle with the hands on the floor, or a two-hand two-foot hop.
how: Feet wide, squat down and put both hands flat on the ground between them.
Hop the hands forward, then hop both feet up to meet them.
Stay low the whole way.
monkey-walk.watch: Standing up between hops. The point is staying down in the squat.

overhand-throw.name: Overhand throw
overhand-throw.short: A full throw over the top of the shoulder, tested for distance with each arm.
how: Side on, weight on the back foot.
Step, turn the hips, then the shoulders, then whip the arm through.
Three throws each arm. Mark the best with a cone and pace it out.
overhand-throw.watch: Throwing from the elbow with a still body. The power comes from the hips turning first.

pivot.name: Pivot
pivot.short: Keeping one foot planted and stepping around it with the other.
how: After a jump stop, pick one foot to be the pivot foot.
Keep that toe glued to the floor.
Step around with the other foot, forward and backward, staying low.
Five each foot.
pivot.watch: The pivot foot sliding or lifting, which is a travel.

pound-dribble.name: Pound dribble
pound-dribble.short: Hard stationary dribbling at about knee height, one hand at a time.
how: Athletic stance, ball to one side of the body.
Push the ball down hard with the fingertips, not the palm.
Twenty five with each hand, eyes up the whole time.
pound-dribble.watch: Slapping with a flat palm, or the ball creeping up above the waist.
pound-dribble.cue: Eyes up, ball low, pound it.

pull-back.name: Pull-back
pull-back.short: Dragging the ball backward with the sole to change direction quickly.
how: Put the sole on top of the ball while moving forward.
Drag it back sharply behind the standing foot.
Turn and go the other way with the next touch.
pull-back.watch: Reaching for it with a straight leg instead of getting the body over the ball.
pull-back.cue: Step on it and drag it home.

rally-count.name: Rally count
rally-count.short: A cooperative rally with Dad where the goal is keeping it going, not winning.
how: Green ball, both trying to make the rally last.
Count every ball over the net out loud.
Best of three attempts. Record the highest.
rally-count.watch: Turning it competitive. Cooperative means both of them are on the same side.
rally-count.cue: How long can we keep it alive?

reaction-start.name: Reaction start
reaction-start.short: A short sprint that begins on a sound or a sight instead of a countdown.
how: Stand in athletic stance facing Dad.
Go on the clap, or on Dad dropping a hand, with no warning.
Sprint 10m. Full rest between reps.
reaction-start.watch: Guessing early. A false start means that rep does not count.

ready-position.name: Ready position
ready-position.short: The athletic stance applied to a sport, waiting for the ball to tell you where to go.
how: Feet wider than the shoulders, knees soft, weight forward on the balls of the feet.
In tennis, racket up in front with both hands on it.
In goal, hands in front at chest height, palms forward, weight on the toes.
ready-position.watch: Standing upright, or hands dropping down by the hips.
ready-position.cue: Hands up, knees soft, nose over toes.

red-light.name: Red Light
red-light.short: The Week 3 challenge: sprint on green, stop in three quiet steps on red.
how: Dad calls green and Teddy sprints.
Dad calls red and Teddy stops in three steps.
Score each stop out of ten for quiet and balance.
Monday number, Friday number.
red-light.watch: Anticipating the call and slowing down early.
red-light.cue: Full speed until you hear it.

safe-fall.name: Safe fall
safe-fall.short: Learning to fall onto the side and forearm instead of onto straight arms.
how: Start from kneeling on grass or a mat.
Tip sideways, tucking the chin and rolling onto the side of the body and the forearm.
Keep the hand open and the arm bent, never reaching out straight.
Five each side, then from a low squat.
safe-fall.watch: Reaching out with a straight arm. That is exactly how wrists break.

scoop.name: Scoop
scoop.short: The goalkeeper's pickup for balls rolling along the ground.
how: Get the body behind the line of the ball.
Bend at the knees and hips with the hands down, little fingers together, palms up.
Scoop it up and pull it into the chest in one movement.
scoop.watch: Bending only at the waist with straight legs, and leaving a gap between the hands and the legs.
scoop.cue: Get behind it, scoop and hug.

shadow-swings.name: Shadow swings
shadow-swings.short: Full strokes swung with no ball, so all the attention goes on the shape.
how: Start in ready position with both hands on the racket.
Make a full unit turn, swing low to high, finish over the shoulder.
Ten forehands, ten backhands, slowly.
Dad watches one thing only per set.
shadow-swings.watch: Rushing them. Slow shadow swings are where the form actually changes.
shadow-swings.cue: Same swing every time, like a stamp.

shake-out.name: Shake out
shake-out.short: The five-minute close to every session: walk, stretch the calves, breathe, write the log line.
how: Walk a slow lap.
Calves against a wall, then hamstrings.
Three slow breaths.
One line in the Champion's Log.
shake-out.watch: Skipping it on good days. It is the habit that protects a tall frame later.
shake-out.cue: Walk it off, breathe, write your line.

sharks-and-minnows.name: Sharks and minnows
sharks-and-minnows.short: A crossing game where the shark tries to tag runners, played this fall with Dad stationary.
how: Mark two safe lines with the shark in the middle.
Dad stays in one spot and rolls balls to tag rather than chasing.
Teddy tries to cross without being hit.
Narrow the field to make it harder.
sharks-and-minnows.watch: Nothing technical. It is change of direction disguised as a game.
sharks-and-minnows.cue: Wait for your moment, then go.

shuffle.name: Shuffle
shuffle.short: Moving sideways staying square, feet never crossing.
how: Start in athletic stance.
Push off the trailing foot and step out with the lead foot.
Bring the trailing foot near but never past the lead foot.
Stay low the whole way.
shuffle.watch: Feet clicking together, standing up tall, or crossing over.
shuffle.cue: Stay wide, stay low, don't let your feet kiss.

silent-landings.name: Silent Landings
silent-landings.short: The Week 1 challenge: ten jumps off a step, counting how many make no sound at all.
how: Find a step or curb and jump off it ten times.
Dad listens with his eyes closed and scores each one silent or not.
Write the Monday number on the chart, try to beat it on Friday.
silent-landings.watch: Quiet comes from bending the knees and landing toes first, then heels.

single-leg-balance.name: Single-leg balance
single-leg-balance.short: Standing on one leg for time, eventually with the eyes closed.
how: Stand on one leg, other knee lifted, arms out.
Eyes open first, up to 60 seconds each leg.
When that is easy, close the eyes. The time will drop a lot, which is normal.
single-leg-balance.watch: Gripping hard with the toes, or the standing knee locking straight.
single-leg-balance.cue: Soft knee, quiet foot, look at one spot.

single-leg-hop.name: Single-leg hop
single-leg-hop.short: Hopping for distance off one leg and landing on that same leg.
how: Stand on one leg behind the line.
Swing the arms and hop forward as far as possible.
Land on the same leg and hold it.
Two trials each leg. Record both legs separately.
single-leg-hop.watch: A gap of more than 15 percent between legs is worth flagging and evening out.
single-leg-hop.cue: Same foot takes off, same foot lands.

single-leg-stick.name: Single-leg stick
single-leg-stick.short: A small hop landed and held on one leg for three seconds.
how: Small hop forward off one leg.
Land on that same leg, knee bending to absorb.
Statue for three seconds before moving.
Five each leg, then five hopping sideways.
single-leg-stick.watch: The knee falling inward on landing, or arms windmilling for balance.

skateboard-cruise.name: Skateboard cruise
skateboard-cruise.short: Unstructured skateboarding, in the program as balance and confidence work rather than a drill.
how: Helmet on, pads if the park is busy.
Cruise, push, turn, stop. Nothing timed and nothing scored.
Finish before he gets tired enough to get sloppy.
skateboard-cruise.watch: Fatigue. Skate first in the session, not last.
skateboard-cruise.cue: Knees soft, look where you are going.

skips.name: Skips
skips.short: Ordinary playground skipping, used here as rhythm and elastic work.
how: Step and hop on the same foot, then step and hop on the other.
Drive the opposite arm up with each knee.
Get taller as it gets easier, not faster.
skips.watch: Flat heavy landings. Skips should sound light.

sole-rolls.name: Sole rolls
sole-rolls.short: Rolling the ball sideways across the body using the sole of one foot.
how: Put the sole of one foot on top of the ball.
Roll it across the body to the other side without losing contact.
Step across and roll it back with the same foot, then switch feet.
Thirty seconds.
sole-rolls.watch: Standing over the ball too upright, or letting the foot slip off the top.

split-step.name: Split step
split-step.short: A tiny hop that lands just as the opponent hits, so you are light and able to go either way.
how: From ready position, hop barely off the ground.
Time it so you land as the other player makes contact.
Land on the balls of both feet, knees soft, then push off in the direction you need.
split-step.watch: A big jump, or landing flat-footed and stuck.

standing-start.name: Standing start
standing-start.short: Starting a sprint from a still standing position, the format used for the 20m test.
how: Toes behind the line, one foot slightly ahead of the other.
Lean forward until you almost fall, then go.
First few steps short and pushing, body low, then rise up gradually.
standing-start.watch: Standing straight up on the first step, or rocking backward before going forward.

step-and-throw.name: Step-and-throw
step-and-throw.short: The foundation throwing pattern: step with the opposite foot, then throw.
how: Stand side on to the target, ball hand back.
Step forward with the foot opposite the throwing arm.
Throw as the front foot lands, letting the hips turn through.
Both arms get volume. The non-dominant one will look bad at first.
step-and-throw.watch: Stepping with the same-side foot, or throwing with only the arm while the feet stay still.
step-and-throw.cue: Opposite foot steps at the target.

stick-landing.name: Stick landing
stick-landing.short: Landing from a jump and freezing completely still, quiet and balanced.
how: Jump up or off a low step.
Land on both feet at the same time, knees bending to absorb it.
Knees over the toes, chest up, hands out in front.
Freeze for three seconds without a wobble or an extra hop.
stick-landing.watch: Knees caving inward, a loud landing, or a small hop after touching down. If the knees cave, lower the step.

three-step-stop.name: Three-step stop
three-step-stop.short: Braking from a run to a complete stop in three quiet steps, under control.
how: Run, then on the signal drop the hips and shorten the steps.
Three steps only: long, shorter, stop.
Finish in athletic stance, balanced, making almost no noise.
three-step-stop.watch: Stiff straight legs, loud slapping feet, or the chest falling forward past the toes.
three-step-stop.cue: Sit down into the brakes, quiet feet.

tick-tocks.name: Tick-tocks
tick-tocks.short: Tapping the ball side to side between the insides of both feet, like a metronome.
how: Ball in front, feet a little wider than the ball.
Push it across with the inside of the right foot.
Push it straight back with the inside of the left foot.
Small taps, steady beat, ankles locked. Thirty seconds.
tick-tocks.watch: The ball drifting further away with each tap, or his head dropping to watch it.

toe-taps.name: Toe taps
toe-taps.short: Tapping the top of a still ball with the sole of alternating feet, quick and light.
how: Ball still on the ground in front of him.
Tap the top of it with the sole of one foot, then hop and tap with the other.
Stay on the balls of the feet and keep a steady quick rhythm.
Thirty seconds.
toe-taps.watch: Standing flat-footed, or the ball rolling away because the taps are too heavy.
toe-taps.cue: Light and fast, like the ball is hot.

touch-then-pass.name: Touch-then-pass
touch-then-pass.short: Receiving with one touch and passing with the next, in a single rhythm.
how: Take the first touch into space, slightly to the side.
Pass with the very next touch.
Count it as one beat: touch, pass. Do not add a third touch.
touch-then-pass.watch: Stopping the ball dead and then setting up. That is three touches, not two.

traveling-rings.name: Traveling rings
traveling-rings.short: The swinging rings in Riverside Park: swing from one ring to the next down the line.
how: Hang from the first ring and swing back and forth to build rhythm.
At the front of the swing, reach the free hand for the next ring.
Dad spots at the hips, not the arms.
Goal is three passes, then five.
traveling-rings.watch: Reaching too early, before the swing is carrying him forward.
traveling-rings.cue: Swing first, then reach at the front.

triple-threat.name: Triple threat
triple-threat.short: The stance holding the ball where shooting, passing or driving are all still possible.
how: Knees bent, feet shoulder width, ball held at the hip on the shooting side.
Elbows out a little, head up, eyes on the basket.
From here he can shoot, pass or go, and the defender cannot tell which.
triple-threat.watch: Standing up straight, or holding the ball out where it can be slapped away.
triple-threat.cue: Low and ready, make them guess.

unit-turn.name: Unit turn
unit-turn.short: Turning the shoulders, hips and racket together as one piece at the start of the stroke.
how: From ready position, turn the shoulders sideways to the net.
The non-hitting hand stays on the racket and points across.
Feet turn too. Everything moves at once, not the arm on its own.
unit-turn.watch: The arm going back while the chest stays facing the net.
unit-turn.cue: Turn like a door, all in one piece.

w-catch.name: W-catch
w-catch.short: The goalkeeper's catch for balls at chest height and above, thumbs together behind the ball.
how: Hands up, thumbs and index fingers almost touching so they make a W.
Meet the ball in front of the face with both hands behind it.
Let the arms give as it arrives, then bring it into the chest.
w-catch.watch: Thumbs apart, which lets the ball through between the hands.

wall-ball.name: Wall ball
wall-ball.short: Any throwing and catching game against a wall, scored or streaked.
how: Throw a ball at the wall and catch the rebound.
Add rules: catch one-handed, clap first, catch after one bounce.
Count the streak or play first to ten against Dad.
wall-ball.watch: Catching against the body instead of with the hands out in front.
wall-ball.cue: Hands out, watch it all the way in.

wall-handstand.name: Wall handstand
wall-handstand.short: Holding a handstand with the feet resting on a wall for support.
how: Hands on the floor about a foot from the wall.
Walk the feet up the wall until the body is close to straight.
Arms locked, head between the arms, belly tight.
Hold for five seconds, build toward ten.
wall-handstand.watch: Arched back with the ribs flaring out, or elbows bending.
wall-handstand.cue: Straight as a pencil, push the floor away.

wall-passes.name: Wall passes
wall-passes.short: Passing against a wall and controlling the rebound, over and over.
how: Stand about three metres from the wall.
Pass with the inside of the foot, control the rebound, pass again.
Alternate feet. For the test, count controlled returns in 30 seconds.
wall-passes.watch: Letting the ball get too far away, or using only the strong foot.
wall-passes.cue: Pass, catch it with your foot, pass again.

wall-rally.name: Wall rally
wall-rally.short: Rallying against a practice wall, counting how many in a row.
how: Stand far enough back that the ball comes to a comfortable height.
Split step every time the ball leaves the wall.
Count the streak out loud and try to beat it.
wall-rally.watch: Standing too close, which turns it into fast blocking instead of real strokes.
wall-rally.cue: Back up, full swing, count out loud.
